answer.answer: Three programmes support micro-enterprises and livelihoods through distinct financial mechanisms: (1) The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) [E01] supports new micro-enterprises in rural and urban areas through margin money subsidies (15-35% of project cost depending on category and location) and bank loans, with maximum project costs of ₹50 lakhs for manufacturing and ₹20 lakhs for services [E03]. (2) PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) [E02] provides collateral-free working capital loans to street vendors in three tranches (₹15,000, ₹25,000, and ₹50,000) with 7% interest subsidy to formalize vendors and enhance their economic opportunities [E02]. (3) PMEGP also allocates 5% of funds for backward and forward linkages [E03] to support awareness, training, and entrepreneurship development programmes [E03]. Together, these schemes use subsidies, concessional loans, and capacity-building to generate employment and support enterprise creation across different beneficiary groups.

claim_to_evidence.claim: PMEGP supports new micro-enterprises through margin money subsidies (15-35% of project cost) and bank loans
PM SVANidhi provides collateral-free working capital loans to street vendors in three tranches with 7% interest subsidy
PMEGP allocates 5% of funds for backward and forward linkages including training and entrepreneurship development
